before: This life was begun without the guide, so everything is already open.
after: You started without the guide, so everything is already open.
why: The working reference's example 8 and the owner's: “This life was begun” was the game describing its own state in the passive. The player started the life; say so.
verified: tests/evidence-g02-life.test.ts and tests/evidence-g29-ui.test.ts assert the new words; the condition (no guide state) is unchanged, and the Guide button isn't shown then, so only a command reaches it.

before: Everything is open on this life. The chapters are there to read in any order.
after: Everything is already open. You can read the chapters in any order.
why: “On this life” is one of the brief's named tics, and “are there to read” is indirect. Two short sentences: what's true, what the player can do.
verified: tests/evidence-g02-life.test.ts, 'on a finished guide missing chapters…', asserts the line on a finished guide.

before: This isn’t open yet. Reading “Drama School” in the guide opens it. [Read About It]
after: This isn’t open yet. Read “Drama School” in the guide to open it. [Read About It]
why: A gerund for a subject described the guide's mechanics; an instruction tells the player what to do, beside the button that does it.
verified: tests/help-mechanics.test.ts, '? on School’s Casting tab…', asserts it; seen on the built app.

after: Show Everything / Show Less (no pressed state)
why: Show Less is the plain partner of Show Everything. The toggle also carried aria-pressed while its name changed, so a screen reader said “Fold It Up, pressed”: the label now says what a press does, as Play and Pause do (defects.md, 1).
verified: tests/help-mechanics.test.ts, 'Show Everything and Show Less name what a press does, with no pressed state', which fails with aria-pressed put back.

before: It’s open now. Try it, or go straight on to “What’s Coming”. The guide picks up there whenever you open it.
after: It’s open now. Press Try It to go and use it, or go straight on to “What’s Coming”. Next time you open the guide, it starts there.
why: It names the button beside it, Try It, rather than echoing it in lower case, and says plainly where the guide opens next time.
verified: tests/help-mechanics.test.ts reads it after every chapter of a new life's guide; follow-1440/log.txt reads it after each of the seventeen chapters on the built app.

before: That was the last chapter, and every part of the game is open. Guide, at the top of the screen, opens any chapter again whenever you want it.
after: That was the last chapter, and every part of the game is open now. To read any chapter again, press Guide at the top of the screen.
why: Lead with what the player can do and the control that does it, not with the button's name as a subject.
verified: tests/help-mechanics.test.ts asserts it; follow-1440/log.txt, chapter life.

why: A gerund phrase as a heading read stiffly. What It Opens says the same beside What It Opened, its read form.
verified: tests/evidence-g02-life.test.ts asserts it on an unfinished guide and its absence on a finished one; follow-1440/log.txt checks it on every chapter.

before: Preparing the work your classes set, table work, how you’ll play a scene, feedback, rehearsing with a partner and working a problem through.
after: Preparing the pieces your classes set, table work, how you’ll play a scene, your teachers’ notes, rehearsing with a partner, your classmates and working a problem through.
why: “The work” is engine-speak for a piece; “feedback” is the glossary's word for what the screen calls your teacher's notes; and the lead left out its entry Your Class.
verified: The help's contents on the built app (follow-1440/help-contents.txt); tests/help-mechanics.test.ts renders it.

after: Being cast, learning a part, the director’s notes, how you’ll play a part, the nights, the Cabaret and plays to read.

before: Your Player Profile, practice, genres, practice briefs, a piece of work explained and your work so far.
after: Your Player Profile, practice, genres, practice briefs from preparing to taping, how a piece was judged, and your work so far.
